title: What is known about 1RB1LF_0RC1RD_1LA1LD_1LE0RA_---1LC_0LA1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LF_0RC1RD_1LA1LD_1LE0RA_---1LC_0LA1LA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and reduced to a map. Lean's kernel proves that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of an explicit two-variable map from (74, 30) reaches one of four exact differences (provided the orbit never meets one of a few small cases, which it does not in 106 rounds). The orbit has been followed for 106 rounds without halting; c then has 306,184 bits, and the chance of a later hit is astronomically small, but no proof is known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 32,377 cells have been visited and 32,373 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.056).

claims.title: The rounds, for all block lengths
claims.text: 28 rules taking one round start A>0 1^x1 0 1^x2 0 ... to the next, each for every value of its counts, generated by py/rules.py with the shared symbolic simulator and checked by Lean; restated on blocks, the main loop (f, m, z) → (f-2, m-2, z+6) iterated by induction, and whole phases.

claims.title: The map
claims.text: From the round start A>0 1^a 0 1^c the machine reaches the round start of mapc a c, or halts when mapc says so: c even: (a-c+12, 3c-6) if c ≤ a+8, halt if c = a+10, a+12, (c-a-10, 3a+27) if c ≥ a+14; c odd: (a-c-1, 3c+6) if c ≤ a-5, halt if c = a-1, a-3, (c-a+3, 3a) if c > a.

claims.title: Halts iff the orbit reaches the halting set
claims.text: Step 6,998 from blank tape is the round start (74, 30) (init_reach). If the orbit of mapc from (74, 30) never meets a case with blocks too short for the rules (.small), the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit reaches .halt.

claims.title: 10<sup>6</sup> rounds of the map: no halt, no small case
claims.text: The orbit from (74, 30), iterated with exact integers for 106 rounds, never reaches .halt or .small; c then has 306,184 bits (growth about ×1.236 a round). The first rounds agree with the machine's own round starts.

claims.title: Probably never halts
claims.text: Halting needs |c − a| to equal one of four small values, while along the orbit |c − a| has about as many bits as c (never more than 26 fewer after round 40). If it behaved like a random number of that size, the chance of a hit after round n would be about Σ 4/c<sub>k</sub>, astronomically small.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known: it would take a proof that the orbit of the map never hits the four exact differences, a Collatz-like question.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, but the question is now a question about a simple map. Started on a blank tape, this machine keeps two blocks of ones on its tape, of lengths a and c; each round replaces (a, c) by a difference and a triple of them. Lean proves it halts exactly when that map hits one of four exact differences. This page runs the real machine and explains the map.

facts.text: The reduction to the map, proved in Lean for all block lengths.
Of the map, with exact integers: no halt; c has 306,184 bits.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.495). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.056).
After 109 steps the tape spans 32,377 cells (23,541 left of the start, 114 right), with a density of 1s of 1.0.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

left986,168,806A>0 1^5334 0 1^20011 0 1^6846

These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Blocks of ones, two or three at a time
html: Between rounds the tape is a few blocks of ones separated by single 0s, with the head in state A on the blank cell just left of them. Write K[x1, x2, ..., xk] for A>0 1^x1 0 1^x2 0 ... 0 1^xk. The head sweeps right across all the blocks and back; each round changes only two or three blocks by a few ones, depending on parities:

round startnext round start
K[f, m, z], f even ≥ 4, m odd ≥ 3K[f−2, m−2, z+6] (the main loop)
K[f, 1, z], f ≥ 6K[f−2, z+9]
K[2, m, z], m ≥ 3K[m+1, z+6]
K[4, 1, z] or K[2, 1, z]halts
K[a, c], both evenK[a, c−4, 9], then the 9 shrinks to 1 in four rounds while the last block gains 6 per round, then merges
K[a, c], c oddK[a−2, c−2, 6]

So with three blocks the first two each lose two ones per round and the last gains six, until the first block is down to 2 or the middle one to 1; then the three blocks become two again. That whole phase is one step of a map on the pair of blocks.

sections.heading: A map on two numbers
html: With two blocks (a, c) (a is always even), one phase gives:

cconditionnext (a, c)
evenc ≤ a + 8(a − c + 12, 3c − 6)
evenc = a + 10 or a + 12halt
evenc ≥ a + 14(c − a − 10, 3a + 27)
oddc ≤ a − 5(a − c − 1, 3c + 6)
oddc = a − 1 or a − 3halt
oddc > a(c − a + 3, 3a)

The new first block is a difference of the old ones and the new second block is three times one of them: a subtractive Euclid algorithm with a factor 3, so c grows by about 1.236 per phase. From blank tape the machine reaches K[74, 30] at step 6,998 and then follows the map:

For example (74, 30): c is even and 30 ≤ 82, so a' = 74 − 30 + 12 = 56 and c' = 3·30 − 6 = 84. On the tape this is the block 9 split off 30, shrunk to 1 and merged (five rounds), then 15 rounds of the main loop (the middle block 15 down to 1, the first block 72 down to 58), then the merge.

sections.heading: Four exact differences
html: Lean proves (all by the kernel) that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit from (74, 30) reaches a halting case, that is c − a = 10 or 12 with c even, or a − c = 1 or 3 with c odd (the first block runs out while the middle one is still there, and the head walks off the left end in state E). The statement assumes the orbit never meets one of a few cases with very short blocks, which it does not in the 106 phases computed.

Along the orbit |c − a| is always about as large as c itself, and c has 306,184 bits after 106 phases. If |c − a| behaved like a random number of that size, the chance of ever hitting one of the four values would be astronomically small. So the machine is very probably a non-halter; a proof would need to control an exact difference along the orbit of a Collatz-like map, and none is known.

summary: Two blocks of ones (a, c) follow a piecewise-linear map with c about tripled each round; Lean proves it halts iff the orbit hits c - a = 10, 12 (c even) or a - c = 1, 3 (c odd); 10^6 rounds miss them.
